Every test config must point somewhere\n543\t    /// private instead.\n544\t    ///\n545\t    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\n546\t    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\n547\t    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\n548\t    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n549\t        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\n550\t        use std::sync::OnceLock;\n551\t\n552\t        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\n553\t        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\n554\t\n555\t        let root =\n556\t            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"failed to create test home root\"));\n557\t        let dir = root\n558\t            .path()\n559\t            .join(format!(\"home-{}\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\n560\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\"state\")).expect(\"failed to create test home state dir\");\n561\t        dir\n562\t    }\n563\t\n564\t    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\n565\t    ///\n566\t    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\n567\t    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\n568\t    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\n569\t    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\n570\t        let lock = ENV_LOCK\n571\t            .lock()\n572\t            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\n573\t        let guard = EnvGuard {\n574\t            saved: GUARDED_VARS\n575\t                .iter()\n576\t                .map(|&key| (key, std::env::var_os(key)))\n577\t                .collect(),\n578\t        };\n579\t        (lock, guard)\n580\t    }\n581\t}\n582\t\n583\t#[cfg(test)]\n584\tmod tests {\n585\t    use super::*;\n586\t    use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};\n587\t    use std::env;\n588\t    use std::path::PathBuf;\n589\t\n590\t ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n376\t\n377\t/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n378\t///\n379\t/// ETXTBSY (\"Text file busy\") occurs when the kernel blocks execution of a binary\n380\t/// that has a write-mode file descriptor still open. This is a genuine race condition:\n381\t///\n382\t/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n383\t/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n384\t/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n385\t/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n386\t///\n387\t/// This is most common with:\n388\t/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n389\t/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n390\t/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n391\t///\n392\t/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n393\t/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n394\t/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n395\t///\n396\t/// # Parameters\n397\t///\n398\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n399\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n400\t/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n401\t///\n402\t/// # Returns\n403\t///\n404\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n405\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n406\t///\n407\t/// # When to use this helper\n408\t///\n409\t/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n410\t/// disk immediately before execution:\n411\t///\n412\t/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n413\t/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n414\t/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n415\t///\n416\t/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n417\t/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n418\t///\n419\t/// # Example\n420\t///\n421\t/// ```no_run\n422\t/// use std::path::Path;\n423\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n424\t///\n425\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n426\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n427\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n428\t///     || async {\n429\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n430\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n431\t///             .output()\n432\t///             .await\n433\t///     },\n434\t///     5,\n435\t///     20,\n436\t/// ).await?;\n437\t/// # Ok(())\n438\t/// # }\n439\t/// ```\n440\tpub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n441\t    spawn_fn: F,\n442\t    max_attempts: u32,\n443\t    backoff_ms: u64,\n444\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n445\twhere\n446\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n447\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n448\t{\n449\t    let mut last_err = None;\n450\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n451\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n452\t            Ok(output) => {\n453\t                if attempt > 0 {\n454\t                    debug!(\n455\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n456\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n457\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n458\t                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n459\t                        attempt + 1\n460\t                    );\n461\t                }\n462\t                return Ok(output);\n463\t            }\n464\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n465\t                last_err = Some(e);\n466\t                warn!(\n467\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n468\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n469\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n470\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n471\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n472\t                    attempt + 1,\n473\t                    max_attempts,\n474\t                    backoff_ms\n475\t Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n482\t}\n483\t\n484\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n515\t/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n516\t/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n517\t///\n518\t/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n519\t/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n520\t/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n521\t/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n522\t///\n523\t/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n524\t/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n525\t/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n526\t/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n527\t/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n528\t/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n529\t///\n530\t/// # Parameters\n531\t///\n532\t/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n533\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n534\t/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n535\t///\n536\t/// # Returns\n537\t///\n538\t/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n539\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n540\t///\n541\t/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n542\t///\n543\t/// Use exponential backoff when:\n544\t/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n545\t/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n546\t/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n547\t///\n548\t/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n549\t/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n550\t/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n551\t/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd prevention\n552\t///\n553\t/// # Example\n554\t///\n555\t/// ```no_run\n556\t/// use std::path::Path;\n557\t/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential;\n558\t///\n559\t/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n560\t/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/freshly-written-binary\");\n561\t/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n562\t///     || async {\n563\t///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n564\t///             .arg(\"--version\")\n565\t///             .output()\n566\t///             .await\n567\t///     },\n568\t///     10,\n569\t/// base_ms: u64,\n578\t) -> std::io::Result<T>\n579\twhere\n580\t    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n581\t    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n582\t{\n583\t    use rand::Rng;\n584\t\n585\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n586\t    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n587\t\n588\t    let mut last_err = None;\n589\t    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n590\t\n591\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n592\t        match spawn_fn().await {\n593\t            Ok(output) => {\n594\t                if attempt > 0 {\n595\t                    debug!(\n596\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n597\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n598\t                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n599\t      // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n609\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n610\t\n611\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n612\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n613\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n614\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n615\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n616\t                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n617\t\n618\t                warn!(\n619\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n620\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n621\t                    delay_ms = delay,\n622\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n623\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n624\t                    attempt + 1,\n625\t                    max_attempts,\n626\t                    delay\n627\t                );\n628\t                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n629\t            }\n630\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n631\t        }\n632\t    }\n633\t\n634\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n635\t}\n636\t\n637\t/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n638\t///\n639\t/// Specialized version of         );\n796\t                }\n797\t                return Ok(output);\n798\t            }\n799\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n800\t                last_err = Some(e);\n801\t\n802\t                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n803\t                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n804\t\n805\t                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n806\t                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n807\t                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n808\t                let delay = exponential_delay\n809\t                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n810\t                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n811\t\n812\t                warn!(\n813\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n814\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n815\t                    delay_ms = delay,\n816\t                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n817\t                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n818\t                    attempt + 1,\n819\t                    max_attempts,\n820\t                    delay\n821\t                );\n822\t                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay));\n823\t            }\n824\t            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n825\t        }\n826\t    }\n827\t\n828\t    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n829\t}\n830\t\n831\t/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n832\t///\n833\t/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential` for subprocess spawns that\n834\t/// return a `std::process::Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n835\t/// process (e.g., for timeout handling) in synchronous contexts.\n836\t///\n837\t/// # Parameters\n838\t///\n839\t/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n840\t/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n841\t/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n842\t///\n843\t/// # Returns\n844\t///\n845\t/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n846\t/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n847\tpub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child<F>(\n848\t    spawn_fn: F,\n849\t    max_attempts: u32,\n850\t    base_ms: u64,\n851\t) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>\n852\twhere\n853\t    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>,\n854\t{\n855\t    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential(spawn_fn, max_attempts, base_ms)\n856\t}\n857\t\n858\t/// Result of a version check.\n859\t#[derive(Debug)]\n860\tpub enum VersionCheck {\n861\t    /// Version is OK or unknown (no known issues).\n862\t    Ok,\n863\t    /// Known-bad version detected with specific issues.\n864\t    KnownBad {\n865\t        version: String,\n866\t        issues: Vec<String>,\n867\t    },\n868\t    /// Version check failed (bf not found, parse error, etc.).\n869\t    Failed { reason: String },\n870\t}\n871\t\n872\t/// Spawn `<br_path> --version>`, retrying briefly on ETXTBSY.\n873\t///\n874\t/// Wraps `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` to handle the specific case of checking\n875\t/// bead-forge version. backend name from a binary's version output.\\n341\\t///\\n342\\t/// Runs the specified binary with the given version command arguments,\\n343\\t/// captures stdout, and extracts the backend name (first word of output).\\n344\\t///\\n345\\t/// This function includes ETXTBSY (errno 26) retry logic to handle the race\\n346\\t/// condition where a binary written to disk immediately before execution\\n347\\t/// transiently reports \\\"Text file busy\\\".\\n348\\t///\\n349\\t/// # Arguments\\n350\\t///\\n351\\t/// * `binary_path` - Path to the binary to execute\\n352\\t/// * `version_args` - Arguments to pass for version check (e.g., `[\\\"--version\\\"]`)\\n353\\t///\\n354\\t/// # Returns\\n355\\t///\\n356\\t/// * `Result<String>` - The extracted backend name, or an error if:\\n357\\t///   - Binary not found\\n358\\t///   - Binary exits with non-zero code\\n359\\t///   - Output is empty or unparseable\\n360\\t///\\n361\\t/// # Examples\\n362\\t///\\n363\\t/// ```no_run\\n364\\t/// use needle::util::parse_backend_name_from_version;\\n365\\t/// use std::path::Path;\\n366\\t///\\n367\\t/// # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\\n368\\t/// let backend = parse_backend_name_from_version(\\n369\\t///     Path::new(\\\"/usr/local/bin/bf\\\"),\\n370\\t///     &[\\\"--version\\\"]\\n371\\t/// )?;\\n372\\t/// assert_eq!(backend, \\\"bf\\\");\\n373\\t/// # Ok(())\\n374\\t/// # }\\n375\\t/// ```\\n376\\tpub fn parse_backend_name_from_version(\\n377\\t    binary_path: &std::path::Path,\\n378\\t    version_args: &[&str],\\n379\\t) -> Result<String> {\\n380\\t    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\\n381\\t    use std::thread;\\n382\\t\\n383\\t    // Check if binary exists\\n384\\t    if !binary_path.exists() {\\n385\\t        anyhow::bail!(\\\"binary not found at {}\\\", binary_path.display());\\n386\\t    }\\n387\\t\\n388\\t    // ETXTBSY retry logic: retry with backoff when the kernel reports \\\"Text file busy\\\"\\n389\\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\\n390\\t    let max_attempts = 5;\\n391\\t    let backoff_ms = 20;\\n392\\t\\n393\\t    let mut last_err = None;\\n394\\t    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\\n395\\t        let result = Command::new(binary_path)\\n396\\t            .args(version_args)\\n397\\t            .stdout(Stdio::piped())\\n398\\t            .stderr(Stdio::piped())\\n399\\t            .output();\\n400\\t\\n401\\t        match result {\\n402\\t            Ok(output) => {\\n403\\t                if attempt > 0 {\\n404\\t                    debug!(\\n405\\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\\n406\\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\\n407\\t                        binary = %binary_path.display(),\\n408\\t                        function = \\\"parse_backend_name_from_version\\\",\\n409\\t                        \\\"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\\\",\\n410\\t                        attempt + 1\\n411\\t                    );\\n412\\t                }\\n413\\t\\n414\\t                // Check exit status\\n415\\t                if !output.status.success() {\\n416\\t                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\\n417\\t                    anyhow::bail!(\\n418\\t                        \\\"binary {} exited with code {}: {}\\\",\\n419\\t                        binary_path.display(),\\n420\\t                        output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\\n421\\t                        stderr.trim()\\n422\\t                    );\\n423\\t                }\\n424\\t\\n425\\t                // Capture stdout\\n426\\t                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\\n427\\t                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\\n428\\t\\n429\\t                // Extract backend name (first word)\\n430\\t                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\\n431\\t                    anyhow::anyhow!(\\n432\\t                        \\\"binary {} produced empty or unparseable version output\\\",\\n433\\t                        binary_path.display()\\n434\\t                    )\\n435\\t                })?;\\n436\\t\\n437\\t                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\\n438\\t            }\\n439\\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\\n440\\t                last_err = Some(e);\\n441\\t                warn!(\\n442\\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\\n443\\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\\n444\\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\\n445\\t                    binary = %binary_path.display(),\\n446\\t                    function = \\\"parse_backend_name_from_version\\\",\\n447\\t                    \\\"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\\\",\\n448\\t                    attempt + 1,\\n449\\t                    max_attempts,\\n450\\t                    backoff_ms\\n451\\t                );\\n452\\t                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\\n453\\t            }\\n454\\t            Err(e) => {\\n455\\t                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\\n456\\t                    format!(\\n457\\t                        \\\"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\\\",\\n458\\t                        binary_path.display(),\\n459\\t                        version_args\\n460\\t                    )\\n461\\t                })\\n462\\t            }\\n463\\t        }\\n464\\t    }\\n465\\t\\n466\\t    // All retries exhausted\\n467\\t    Err(last_err.expect(\\\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\\\")).with_context(\\n468\\t        || {\\n469\\t            format!(\\n470\\t                \\\"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\\\",\\n471\\t                binary_path.display(),\\n472\\t                max_attempts\\n473\\t            )\\n474\\t        },\\n475\\t    )\\n476\\t}\\n477\\t\\n478\\t/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\\n479\\t///\\n480\\t/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\\n481\\t/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\\\"HOME\\\", ..)` or\\n482\\t/// `remove_var(\\\"HOME\\\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\\n483\\t/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\\n484\\t/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\\n485\\t/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\\n486\\t/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\\n487\\t/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\\n488\\t///\\n489\\t/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\\n490\\t/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\\n491\\t/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\\n492\\t#[cfg(test)]\\n493\\tpub(crate) mod test_env {\\n494\\t    use std::ffi::OsString;\\n495\\t    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\\n496\\t\\n497\\t    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\\n498\\t    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\\n499\\t\\n500\\t    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\\n501\\t    ///\\n502\\t    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\\n503\\t    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\\n504\\t    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\\n505\\t    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\\n506\\t    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\\n507\\t    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\\n508\\t    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\\n509\\t        \\\"HOME\\\",\\n510\\t        \\\"PATH\\\",\\n511\\t        \\\"NEEDLE_HOME\\\",\\n512\\t        \\\"NEEDLE_EVENTS\\\",\\n513\\t        \\\"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\\\",\\n514\\t    ];\\n515\\t\\n516\\t    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\\n517\\t    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\\n518\\t        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\\n519\\t    }\\n520\\t\\n521\\t    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\\n522\\t        fn drop(&mut self) {\\n523\\t            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\\n524\\t                restore(key, value);\\n525\\t            }\\n526\\t        }\\n527\\t    }\\n528\\t\\n529\\t    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\\n530\\t        match value {\\n531\\t            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\\n532\\t            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\\n533\\t        }\\n534\\t    }\\n535\\t\\n536\\t    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\\n537\\t    ///\\n538\\t    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\\n539\\t    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\\n540\\t    /// registry. Unit tests that construct a `Worker` therefore registered\\n541\\t    /// themselves into it and raced each other (and the running fleet) on a\\n542\\t    /// single read-modify-write file. Every test config must point somewhere\\n543\\t    /// private instead.\\n544\\t    ///\\n545\\t    /// Each call returns a fresh subdirectory, so concurrently running tests\\n546\\t    /// that share a worker id never touch the same registry file. The backing\\n547\\t    /// root is held in a `OnceLock` for the lifetime of the test process.\\n548\\t    pub(crate) fn isolated_home() -> std::path::PathBuf {\\n549\\t        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};\\n550\\t        use std::sync::OnceLock;\\n551\\t\\n552\\t        static ROOT: OnceLock<tempfile::TempDir> = OnceLock::new();\\n553\\t        static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);\\n554\\t\\n555\\t        let root =\\n556\\t            ROOT.get_or_init(|| tempfile::tempdir().expect(\\\"failed to create test home root\\\"));\\n557\\t        let dir = root\\n558\\t            .path()\\n559\\t            .join(format!(\\\"home-{}\\\", NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)));\\n560\\t        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join(\\\"state\\\")).expect(\\\"failed to create test home state dir\\\");\\n561\\t        dir\\n562\\t    }\\n563\\t\\n564\\t    /// Acquire the environment lock and capture `HOME`/`PATH` for restoration.\\n565\\t    ///\\n566\\t    /// Hold the returned tuple for the whole test body; dropping it releases\\n567\\t    /// the lock and restores the environment. The lock is intentionally\\n568\\t    /// poison-tolerant: a panicking test must not wedge every later test.\\n569\\t    pub(crate) fn isolate_env() -> (MutexGuard<'static, ()>, EnvGuard) {\\n570\\t        let lock = ENV_LOCK\\n571\\t            .lock()\\n572\\t            .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());\\n573\\t        let guard = EnvGuard {\\n574\\t            saved: guard)\\n580\\t    }\\n581\\t}\\n582\\t\\n583\\t#[cfg(test)]\\n584\\tmod tests {\\n585\\t    use super::*;\\n586\\t    use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike};\\n587\\t    use std::env;\\n588\\t    use Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\\n335\\t            \\\"chrono operation panicked - possibly due to extreme system clock values\\\"\\n336\\t        )),\\n337\\t    }\\n338\\t}\\n339\\t\\n340\\t/// Parse the backend name from a binary's version output.\\n341\\t///\\n342\\t/// Runs the specified binary with the given version command arguments,\\n343\\t/// captures stdout, and extracts the backend name (first word of output).\\n344\\t///\\n345\\t/// This function includes ETXTBSY (errno 26) retry logic to handle the race\\n346\\t/// condition where a binary written to disk immediately before execution\\n347\\t/// transiently reports \\\"Text file busy\\\".\\n348\\t///\\n349\\t/// # Arguments\\n350\\t///\\n351\\t/// * `binary_path` - Path to the binary to execute\\n352\\t/// * `version_args` - Arguments to pass for version check (e.g., `[\\\"--version\\\"]`)\\n353\\t///\\n354\\t/// # Returns\\n355\\t///\\n356\\t/// * `Result<String>` - The extracted backend name, or an error if:\\n357\\t///   - Binary not found\\n358\\t///   - Binary exits with non-zero code\\n359\\t///   - Output is empty or unparseable\\n360\\t///\\n361\\t/// # Examples\\n362\\t///\\n363\\t/// ```no_run\\n364\\t/// use needle::util::parse_backend_name_from_version;\\n365\\t/// use std::path::Path;\\n366\\t///\\n367\\t/// # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\\n368\\t/// let backend = {\\n380\\t    use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\\n381\\t    use std::thread;\\n382\\t\\n383\\t    // Check if binary exists\\n384\\t    if !binary_path.exists() {\\n385\\t busy\\\"\\n389\\t    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\\n390\\t    let max_attempts = 5;\\n391\\t    let backoff_ms = 20;\\n392\\t\\n393\\t    let mut last_err = None;\\n394\\t    for attempt in debug!(\\n405\\t                        attempt = attempt + 1,\\n406\\t                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\\n407\\t                        binary = %binary_path.display(),\\n408\\t                        function = \\\"parse_backend_name_from_version\\\",\\n409\\t                        \\\"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\\\",\\n410\\t                        attempt + 1\\n411\\t                    );\\n412\\t                }\\n413\\t\\n414\\t                // Check exit status\\n415\\t                if !output.status.success() {\\n416\\t                    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\\n417\\t                    anyhow::bail!(\\n418\\t                        \\\"binary {} exited with code {}: {}\\\",\\n419\\t                        binary_path.display(),\\n420\\t                        output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),\\n421\\t                        stderr.trim()\\n422\\t                    );\\n423\\t                }\\n424\\t\\n425\\t                // Capture stdout\\n426\\t                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\\n427\\t                let trimmed_output = stdout.trim();\\n428\\t\\n429\\t                // Extract backend name (first word)\\n430\\t                let backend_name = trimmed_output.split_whitespace().next().ok_or_else(|| {\\n431\\t                    anyhow::anyhow!(\\n432\\t                        \\\"binary {} produced empty or unparseable version output\\\",\\n433\\t                        binary_path.display()\\n434\\t                    )\\n435\\t                })?;\\n436\\t\\n437\\t                return Ok(backend_name.to_string());\\n438\\t            }\\n439\\t            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\\n440\\t                last_err = Some(e);\\n441\\t                warn!(\\n442\\t                    attempt = attempt + 1,\\n443\\t                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\\n444\\t                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\\n445\\t                    binary = %binary_path.display(),\\n446\\t                    function = \\\"parse_backend_name_from_version\\\",\\n447\\t                    \\\"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\\\",\\n448\\t                    attempt + 1,\\n449\\t                    max_attempts,\\n450\\t                    backoff_ms\\n451\\t                );\\n452\\t                thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\\n453\\t            }\\n454\\t            Err(e) => {\\n455\\t                return Err(e).with_context(|| {\\n456\\t                    format!(\\n457\\t                        \\\"failed to execute binary {} with version args {:?}\\\",\\n458\\t                        binary_path.display(),\\n459\\t                        version_args\\n460\\t                    )\\n461\\t                })\\n462\\t            }\\n463\\t        }\\n464\\t    }\\n465\\t\\n466\\t    // All retries exhausted\\n467\\t    Err(last_err.expect(\\\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\\\")).with_context(\\n468\\t        || {\\n469\\t            format!(\\n470\\t                \\\"failed to execute binary {} after {} attempts (ETXTBSY)\\\",\\n471\\t                binary_path.display(),\\n472\\t                max_attempts\\n473\\t            )\\n474\\t        },\\n475\\t    )\\n476\\t}\\n477\\t\\n478\\t/// Crate-wide test-only environment isolation.\\n479\\t///\\n480\\t/// `HOME` is process-global, but Rust runs unit tests as threads inside a\\n481\\t/// single process. Any test that calls `set_var(\\\"HOME\\\", ..)` or\\n482\\t/// `remove_var(\\\"HOME\\\")` therefore mutates state that every concurrently\\n483\\t/// running test observes. Before this module existed, several modules each\\n484\\t/// had their own private `Mutex` (or none at all), which provides no mutual\\n485\\t/// exclusion against the others — tests that merely *read* `HOME`\\n486\\t/// (`worker::tests`, `telemetry::tests`, tilde expansion) failed\\n487\\t/// nondeterministically depending on interleaving.\\n488\\t///\\n489\\t/// Every test that reads or writes `HOME`/`PATH` must go through\\n490\\t/// [`isolate_env`] or [`isolate_env_with_home`] so that exactly one such test\\n491\\t/// runs at a time and the previous values are always restored.\\n492\\t#[cfg(test)]\\n493\\tpub(crate) mod test_env {\\n494\\t    use std::ffi::OsString;\\n495\\t    use std::sync::{Mutex, MutexGuard};\\n496\\t\\n497\\t    /// The single process-wide lock guarding `HOME`/`PATH` in tests.\\n498\\t    static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());\\n499\\t\\n500\\t    /// Variables guarded by [`isolate_env`].\\n501\\t    ///\\n502\\t    /// Concurrent `set_var` corrupts the process environment for every\\n503\\t    /// thread — including `Command` spawns reading `PATH`, which is how an\\n504\\t    /// unrelated test's `git` invocation dies with `NotFound` while some\\n505\\t    /// other test mutates an env var (observed in CI: needle-ci-wbgtb,\\n506\\t    /// commit_hook::concurrent_inject_never_cross_tags). Any test mutating\\n507\\t    /// one of these must hold the lock for its whole body.\\n508\\t    const GUARDED_VARS: [&str; 5] = [\\n509\\t        \\\"HOME\\\",\\n510\\t        \\\"PATH\\\",\\n511\\t        \\\"NEEDLE_HOME\\\",\\n512\\t        \\\"NEEDLE_EVENTS\\\",\\n513\\t        \\\"NEEDLE_HEARTBEATS\\\",\\n514\\t    ];\\n515\\t\\n516\\t    /// Restores every guarded variable to its captured value when dropped.\\n517\\t    pub(crate) struct EnvGuard {\\n518\\t        saved: Vec<(&'static str, Option<OsString>)>,\\n519\\t    }\\n520\\t\\n521\\t    impl Drop for EnvGuard {\\n522\\t        fn drop(&mut self) {\\n523\\t            for (key, value) in self.saved.drain(..) {\\n524\\t                restore(key, value);\\n525\\t            }\\n526\\t        }\\n527\\t    }\\n528\\t\\n529\\t    fn restore(key: &str, value: Option<OsString>) {\\n530\\t        match value {\\n531\\t            Some(value) => std::env::set_var(key, value),\\n532\\t            None => std::env::remove_var(key),\\n533\\t        }\\n534\\t    }\\n535\\t\\n536\\t    /// A private, per-caller NEEDLE home for tests.\\n537\\t    ///\\n538\\t    /// `WorkspaceConfig::default_home()` resolves to the operator's real\\n539\\t    /// `~/.needle`, whose `state/workers.json` is the *live fleet's* worker\\n540\\t    /// registry. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_f580b402b5ea4d37bbbbc179","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t![NEEDLE](docs/hero.png)\n2\t\n3\t# 🧵 NEEDLE\n4\t\n5\t[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\n6\t[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)\n7\t[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.4.0-green.svg)](Cargo.toml)\n8\t\n9\t**N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\n10\t\n11\t> Deterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\n12\t\n13\tNEEDLE is a universal wrapper for headless coding CLI agents. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## 🚀 Quickstart\n18\t\n19\t```bash\n20\t# Install the latest release (prebuilt binary, Linux x86_64/aarch64)\n21\tcurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\n22\t\n23\t# Or build from source (needs Rust 1.75+, see rust-toolchain.toml)\n24\tcargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\n25\t\n26\t# Configure your bead workspace backend (required)\n27\tcd /path/to/your/workspace\n28\tcat > .needle.yaml << 'EOF'\n29\tbead_cli:\n30\t  backend: bead-rs  # or 'bead-forge' for legacy bf/br workspaces\n31\tEOF\n32\t\n33\t# Run a worker\n34\tneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\n35\t```\n36\t\n37\tThe installer drops `needle` in `~/.local/bin` (override with `NEEDLE_INSTALL_PATH`);\n38\tmake sure that directory is on your `PATH`.\n39\t\n40\tA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\n41\t\n42\tSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\n43\t\n44\t---\n45\t\n46\t## 🧶 What is a bead?\n47\t\n48\tA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\n49\t\n50\tBeads live in a **bead store** — a pluggable backend managed by a bead CLI. The current primary backend is **bead-rs**, which uses a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a checkpoint directory (`.beads/checkpoint/` with `current.json`, `forensic.jsonl`, and `objects/`). The legacy **bead-forge** backend uses `issues.jsonl`.\n51\t\n52\t```bash\n53\t# Create a bead (bead-rs backend)\n54\tbead create --title \"Add pagination to search results\" --priority 2 --issue-type task\n55\t\n56\t# List open beads\n57\tbead list --status open\n58\t\n59\t# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\n60\t```\n61\t\n62\tNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\n63\t\n64\t---\n65\t\n66\t## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\n67\t\n68\tExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\n69\t\n70\t- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\n71\t- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\n72\t\n73\tNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\n74\t\n75\t---\n76\t\n77\t## 🧠 Core Principle\n78\t\n79\tNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\n80\t\n81\t```\n82\tIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\n83\tIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\n84\t```\n85\t\n86\t---\n87\t\n88\t## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\n89\t\n90\tA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\n91\t\n92\t```\n93\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n94\t│                                                     │\n95\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n96\t│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\n97\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\n98\t│         │                                        │  │\n99\t│         ▼                                        │  │\n100\t│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"call_cfd58a01014c446ea2a8c13f","session_id":"d44287bc-2fed-429c-851a-b9c0131ba397","uuid":"23b29db8-1a8d-4c86-9526-58dc6b16b72b","timestamp":"2026-08-21T23:05:23.838Z","subagent_type":"Explore","task_description":"Explore NEEDLE codebase structure"}
